name: Ivory-backed Woodswallow
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including lembeh (off northeast), and banggai and sula islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A chunky slate-gray and white bird with a heavy, pale blue bill. A gregarious bird of forest and forest edge in the lowlands and mountains.

name: White-collared Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais and espírito santo to eastern santa catarina)
description: Large foliage-gleaner with a wedge-shaped bill. Found in the middle and lower levels of forests with bamboo where it acrobatically hangs upside-down on branches and searches for prey in clusters of dead leaves.

name: Harlequin Antbird
rangeDescription: Eastern amazonian brazil (near west bank of lower rio tapajós)
description: Striking antbird with a cinnamon breast band and a bare eyering. Males have gray underparts, while females have buff underparts scaled with black.

name: Russet-bellied Spinetail
rangeDescription: West slope of andes of central peru (ancash)
description: Uncommon and endangered spinetail with a very small range in the western Andes of Peru. It has a gray head and back, a pale throat, buffy-chestnut lower underparts, a broken white eye-ring, and a long, rusty-edged tail.

name: Jandaya Parakeet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northeastern brazil (eastern pará and goiás to alagoas)
description: Strikingly colored parakeet with a yellow head and chest, orange around the eyes and bill, orange on the belly, and blue flight feathers. Highly gregarious and noisy; can be seen flying over forests, woodlands, and agricultural areas, as well as in cities.

name: Strange-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Striking flycatcher with a spectacular mating display, in which male flies high into the air and repeatedly pumps tails above and then below body. Endemic to the Iberá marshes of NE Argentina and E Paraguay.

name: Rufous-bellied Antwren
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny resident of tall rainforest. Wary and can be difficult to see well; note distinctive sputtering alarm call, tiny size, plain face, and large white (male) or buffy (female) wing spots.

name: Northern Black-throated Trogon
rangeDescription: Northern honduras to far northwestern colombia
description: Yellow-bellied trogon with pale blue eyering and yellowish bill. Male has shimmering green-blue upperparts and chest; female is brown.

name: Western Swamphen
rangeDescription: Iberian peninsula and northwestern africa (morocco to tunisia)
description: Distinctive large waterbird, much larger than a moorhen. Deep purplish-blue overall with a very stout red bill, reddish legs, and a white undertail patch.

name: Rodrigues Fody
rangeDescription: Rodrigues (eastern mascarene islands)
description: A sparrow-like weaver. The mostly yellow breeding males are distinctive, but females and non-breeding males are drab.

name: Great Xenops
rangeDescription: Arid caatinga of interior northeastern and east-central brazil
description: Large and subtly beautiful xenops with a pointy curved bill. Has bright rusty plumage with a white throat.

name: Chestnut-bellied Seedeater
rangeDescription: The guianas and southern venezuela to northern and central bolivia (pando to eastern cochabamba) and amazonian brazil
description: The gray-and-red seedeater of lowland Amazonia. Males are gray with chestnut throat and breast, and are unlikely to be confused with any other seedeater species in their range; females are tawny yellowish, warmer-colored than other female seedeaters in their range but still very similar.

name: Banded Stilt
rangeDescription: Inland salt lakes of southwestern and south-central australia
description: Large black-and-white shorebird with white head and long straight, needle-like bill, very long pink legs. Adult has prominent copper-colored belly-band, lacking in juvenile.

name: Oriental Stork
rangeDescription: Siberia, manchuria, and korea; winters to southern china and northern india
description: Endangered stork of expansive wetlands and fields in East Asia. Adult white with sharply contrasting black flight feathers, black bill, and red legs; juvenile similar but orange-billed.

name: Dickinson's Kestrel
rangeDescription: Palms and savanna of east-central and northeastern south africa
description: Medium-sized gray kestrel. Note the pale head, rump, and underwing, which are conspicuous in flight.

name: Maroon-fronted Parrot
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern mexico (sierra madre oriental)
description: Very local, long-tailed, and social parrot of mountains endemic to northeast Mexico. Feeds in pine and pine-oak forests and adjacent semiopen areas with orchards and flowering century plants.

name: Little Raven
rangeDescription: Southeastern australia (northern new south wales to victoria and eyre peninsula, south australia)
description: Australian crows and ravens are challenging to identify; concentrate on call, throat-hackles, behavior, and location. Calls usually fairly fast and lack the drawn-out wail typical of Australian Raven.

name: Erckel's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Northeastern sudan and highlands of northern eritrea and northwestern ethiopia; introduced to hawaii
description: A pheasant-sized game bird with a chestnut crown, white throat, and white streaks above and below. Males are larger than females.

name: White-lined Antbird
rangeDescription: Far southwestern amazonian brazil to southeastern peru and northwestern bolivia
description: Large antbird of bamboo stands in river edge forest. Males are dark gray with bright white wing bars and a darker blackish crest that is raised when agitated; females appear two-toned: orange above, with creamy white face and underparts.

name: Brown Violetear
rangeDescription: Belize and guatemala to the guianas, brazil, and bolivia
description: Uncommon, rather large but drab, fairly short-billed hummingbird of tropical and subtropical forest and edge. Can be aggressive when defending flower patches from most other hummingbirds.
